entries.f2f9260d71a4d80370858675b860b02fbd8568cf: <div sID="gen3040" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="18" osisID="Num.18" sID="Num.18"/> <div eID="gen3040" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3041" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen3042" type="x-p"/> Aaron being now fully established in the priesthood abundantly to his own satisfaction, and to the satisfaction of the people (which was the good that God brought out of the evil opposition made to him), in this chapter God gives him full instructions concerning his office or rather repeats those which he had before given him. He tells him, I. What must be his work and the care and charge committed to him, and what assistance he should have the Levites in that work, <reference osisRef="Num.18.1-Num.18.7">ver. 1-7</reference>. II. What should be his and the Levites' wages for this work. 1. The perquisites or fees peculiar to the priests, <reference osisRef="Num.18.8-Num.18.19">ver. 8-19</reference>. 2. The settled maintenance of the Levites, <reference osisRef="Num.18.20-Num.18.24">ver. 20-24</reference>. III. The portion which must be paid to the priests out of the Levites' maintenance, <reference osisRef="Num.18.25-Num.18.32">ver. 25-32</reference>. Thus every one knew what he had to do, and what he had to live upon.
entries.a604b23f45c8f84d7b740e37a9f304b237af6518: <div eID="gen3042" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen3041" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Service of the Priests and Levites. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1490.)</title> <div sID="gen3043" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> said unto Aaron, Thou and thy sons and thy father's house with thee shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary: and thou and thy sons with thee shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood. <hi type="super">2</hi> And thy brethren also of the tribe of Levi, the tribe of thy father, bring thou with thee, that they may be joined unto thee, and minister unto thee: but thou and thy sons with thee <hi type="italic">shall minister</hi> before the tabernacle of witness. <hi type="super">3</hi> And they shall keep thy charge, and the charge of all the tabernacle: only they shall not come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, that neither they, nor ye also, die. <hi type="super">4</hi> And they shall be joined unto thee, and keep the charge of the tabernacle of the congregation, for all the service of the tabernacle: and a stranger shall not come nigh unto you. <hi type="super">5</hi> And ye shall keep the charge of the sanctuary, and the charge of the altar: that there be no wrath any more upon the children of Israel. <hi type="super">6</hi> And I, behold, I have taken your brethren the Levites from among the children of Israel: to you <hi type="italic">they are</hi> given <hi type="italic">as</hi> a gift for the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. <hi type="super">7</hi> Therefore thou and thy sons with thee shall keep your priest's office for every thing of the altar, and within the vail; and ye shall serve: I have given your priest's office <hi type="italic">unto you</hi> as a service of gift: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. <div eID="gen3043" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3044" type="x-p"/> The coherence of this chapter with that foregoing is very observable. <div eID="gen3044" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3045" type="x-p"/> I. The people, in the close of that chapter, had complained of the difficulty and peril that there were in drawing near to God, which put them under some dreadful apprehensions that the tabernacle in the midst of them, which they hoped would have been their joy and glory, would rather be their terror and ruin. Now, in answer to this complaint, God here gives them to understand by Aaron that the priests should come near for them as their representatives; so that, though the people were obliged to keep their distance, yet that should not at all redound to their disgrace or prejudice, but their comfortable communion with God should be kept up by the interposition of the priests. <div eID="gen3045" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3046" type="x-p"/> II. A great deal of honour God had now lately put upon Aaron; his rod had budded and blossomed, when the rods of the rest of the princes remained dry, and destitute both of fruit and ornament. Now lest Aaron should be puffed up with the abundance of the favours that were done him, and the miracles that were wrought for the support of him in his high station, God comes to him to remind him of the burden that was laid upon him, and the duty required from him as a priest. He would see reason not to be proud of his preferment, but to receive the honours of his office with reverence and holy trembling, when he considered how great was the charge committed to him, and how hard it would be for him to give a good account of it. <hi type="italic">Be not high-minded, but fear.</hi> <div eID="gen3046" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3047" type="x-p"/> 1. God tells him of the danger that attended his dignity, <reference osisRef="Num.18.1">v. 1</reference>. (1.) That both the priests and Levites (<hi type="italic">thou, and thy sons, and thy father's house</hi>) should <hi type="italic">bear the iniquity of the sanctuary;</hi> that is, if the sanctuary were profaned by the intrusion of strangers, or persons in their uncleanness, the blame should lie upon the Levites and priests, who ought to have kept them off. Though the sinner that thrust in presumptuously should die in his iniquity, yet his blood should be required at the hands of the watchmen. Or it may be taken more generally: "If any of the duties or offices of the sanctuary be neglected, if any service be not done in its season or not according to the law, if any thing be lost or misplaced in the removal of the sanctuary, you shall be accountable for it, and answer it at your peril." (2.) That the priests should themselves <hi type="italic">bear the iniquity of the priesthood;</hi> that is, if they either neglected any part of their work or permitted any other persons to invade their office, and take their work out of their hands, they should bear the blame of it. Note, The greater the trust is of work and power that is committed to us the greater is our danger of contracting guilt, by falsifying and betraying that trust. This is a good reason why we should neither be envious at others' honours nor ambitious ourselves of high places, because great dignity exposes us to great iniquity. Those that are entrusted with the charge of the sanctuary will have a great deal to answer for. Who would covet the care of souls who considers the account that must be given of that care? <div eID="gen3047" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3048" type="x-p"/> 2. He tells him of the duty that attended his dignity. (1.) That he and his sons must <hi type="italic">minister before the tabernacle of witness</hi> (<reference osisRef="Num.18.2">v. 2</reference>); that is (as bishop Patrick explains it), <hi type="italic">before the most holy place,</hi> in which the ark was, on the outside of the veil of that tabernacle, but within the door of the tabernacle, of the congregation. They were to attend the golden altar, the table, and candlestick, which no Levite might approach to. <hi type="italic">You shall serve,</hi> <reference osisRef="Num.18.7">v. 7</reference>. Not, "You shall rule" (it was never intended that they should lord it over God's heritage), but "You shall serve God and the congregation." Note, The priesthood is a service. <hi type="italic">If any desire the office of a bishop he desires a good work.</hi> Ministers must remember that they are ministers, that is, servants, of whom it is required that they be humble, diligent, and faithful. (2.) That the Levites must assist him and his sons, and minister to them in all the <hi type="italic">service of the tabernacle</hi> (<reference osisRef="Num.18.2-Num.18.4">v. 2-4</reference>), though they must by no means come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary, nor at the altar meddle with the great services of burning the fat and sprinkling the blood. Aaron's family was very small, and, as it increased, the rest of the families of Israel would increase likewise, so that the hands of the priests neither were now nor were likely to be sufficient for all the service of the tabernacle; therefore (says God) <hi type="italic">the Levites shall be joined to thee,</hi> <reference osisRef="Num.18.2">v. 2</reference>, and again <reference osisRef="Num.18.4">v. 4</reference>, where there seems to be an allusion to the name of Levi, which signifies <hi type="italic">joined.</hi> Many of the Levites had of late set themselves against Aaron, but henceforward God promises that they should be heartily joined to him in interest and affection, and should no more contest with him. It was a good sign to Aaron that God owned him when he inclined the hearts of those concerned to own him too. The Levites are said to be given as a gift to the priests, <reference osisRef="Num.18.6">v. 6</reference>. Note, We are to value it as a great gift of the divine bounty to have those joined to us that will be helpful and serviceable to us in the service of God. (3.) That both priests and Levites must carefully watch against the profanation of sacred things. The Levites must <hi type="italic">keep the charge of the tabernacle,</hi> that <hi type="italic">no stranger</hi> (that is, none who upon any account was forbidden to come) might <hi type="italic">come nigh</hi> (<reference osisRef="Num.18.4">v. 4</reference>), and that upon pain of death, <reference osisRef="Num.18.7">v. 7</reference>. And the priests must <hi type="italic">keep the charge of the sanctuary</hi> (<reference osisRef="Num.18.5">v. 5</reference>), must instruct the people, and admonish them concerning the due distance they were to keep, and not suffer them to break the bounds set them, as Korah's company had done, that there be <hi type="italic">no wrath any more upon the children of Israel.</hi> Note, The preventing of sin is the preventing of wrath; and the mischief sin has done should be a warning to us for the future to watch against it both in ourselves and others.
entries.9db365b40e857bb07735cf65b70a9547a63cd691: <div eID="gen3048" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3049" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">8</hi> And the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> spake unto Aaron, Behold, I also have given thee the charge of mine heave offerings of all the hallowed things of the children of Israel; unto thee have I given them by reason of the anointing, and to thy sons, by an ordinance for ever. <hi type="super">9</hi> This shall be thine of the most holy things, <hi type="italic">reserved</hi> from the fire: every oblation of theirs, every meat offering of theirs, and every sin offering of theirs, and every trespass offering of theirs, which they shall render unto me, <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> most holy for thee and for thy sons. <hi type="super">10</hi> In the most holy <hi type="italic">place</hi> shalt thou eat it; every male shall eat it: it shall be holy unto thee. <hi type="super">11</hi> And this <hi type="italic">is</hi> thine; the heave offering of their gift, with all the wave offerings of the children of Israel: I have given them unto thee, and to thy sons and to thy daughters with thee, by a statute for ever: every one that is clean in thy house shall eat of it. <hi type="super">12</hi> All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the wheat, the firstfruits of them which they shall offer unto the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , them have I given thee. <hi type="super">13</hi> <hi type="italic">And</hi> whatsoever is first ripe in the land, which they shall bring unto the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , shall be thine; every one that is clean in thine house shall eat <hi type="italic">of</hi> it. <hi type="super">14</hi> Every thing devoted in Israel shall be thine. <hi type="super">15</hi> Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, which they bring unto the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , <hi type="italic">whether it be</hi> of men or beasts, shall be thine: nevertheless the firstborn of man shalt thou surely redeem, and the firstling of unclean beasts shalt thou redeem. 16 And those that are to be redeemed from a month old shalt thou redeem, according to thine estimation, for the money of five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> twenty gerahs. <hi type="super">17</hi> But the firstling of a cow, or the firstling of a sheep, or the firstling of a goat, thou shalt not redeem; they <hi type="italic">are</hi> holy: thou shalt sprinkle their blood upon the altar, and shalt burn their fat <hi type="italic">for</hi> an offering made by fire, for a sweet savour unto the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">18</hi> And the flesh of them shall be thine, as the wave breast and as the right shoulder are thine. <hi type="super">19</hi> All the heave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer unto the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , have I given thee, and thy sons and thy daughters with thee, by a statute for ever: it <hi type="italic">is</hi> a covenant of salt for ever before the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> unto thee and to thy seed with thee. <div eID="gen3049" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3050" type="x-p"/> The priest's service is called a <hi type="italic">warfare;</hi> and who goes a warfare at his own charges? As they were well employed, so they were well provided for, and well paid. None shall serve God for nought. All believers are spiritual priests, and God has promised to take care of them; they shall <hi type="italic">dwell in the land,</hi> and <hi type="italic">verily they shall be fed,</hi> and shall not <hi type="italic">want any good thing.</hi> Godliness has the <hi type="italic">promise of the life that now is.</hi> And from this plentiful provision here made for the priests the apostle infers that it is the duty of Christian churches to maintain their ministers; those that <hi type="italic">served at the altar lived upon the altar.</hi> So those that preach the gospel should <hi type="italic">live upon the gospel,</hi> and live comfortably, <reference osisRef="1Cor.9.13-1Cor.9.14">1 Cor. ix. 13, 14</reference>. Scandalous maintenance makes scandalous ministers. Now observe, 1. That much of the provision that was made for them arose out of the sacrifices which they themselves were employed to offer. They had the skins of almost all the sacrifices, which they might sell, and they had a considerable share out of the meat-offerings, sin-offerings, &c. Those that had the charge of the offerings had the benefit, <reference osisRef="Num.18.8">v. 8</reference>. Note, God's work is its own wages, and his service carries its recompence along with it. Even in keeping God's commandments there is great reward. The present pleasures of religion are part of its pay. 2. That they had not only a good table kept for them, but money likewise in their pockets for the redemption of the first-born, and those firstlings of cattle which might not be offered in sacrifice. Thus their maintenance was such as left them altogether <hi type="italic">disentangled from the affairs of this life;</hi> they had no grounds to occupy, no land to till, no vineyards to dress, no cattle to tend, no visible estate to take care of, and yet had a more plentiful income than any other families whatsoever. Thus God ordered it that they might be the more entirely addicted to their ministry, and not diverted from it, nor disturbed in it, by any worldly care or business (the ministry requires a whole man); and that they might be examples of living by faith, not only in God's providence, but in his ordinance. They lived from hand to mouth, that they might learn to take no thought for the morrow; sufficient for the day would be the provision thereof: and they had no estates to leave their children, that they might by faith leave their children, that they might by faith leave them to the care of that God who had <hi type="italic">fed them all their lives long.</hi> 3. Of the provision that was made for their tables some is said to be <hi type="italic">most holy</hi> (<reference osisRef="Num.18.9-Num.18.10">v. 9, 10</reference>), which was to be eaten by the priests themselves, and in the court of the tabernacle only; but other perquisites were less holy, of which their families might eat, at their own houses, provided they were clean, <reference osisRef="Num.18.11-Num.18.13">v. 11-13</reference>. See <reference osisRef="Lev.21.10-Lev.21.12">Lev. xxi. 10</reference>, &c. 4. It is commanded that the <hi type="italic">best of the oil,</hi> and <hi type="italic">the best of the wine and wheat,</hi> should be offered for the <hi type="italic">first-fruits unto the Lord,</hi> which the priest were to have, <reference osisRef="Num.18.12">v. 12</reference>. Note, We must always serve and honour God with the best we have, for he is the best, and best deserves it; he is the first, and therefore must have the first ripe. Those that think to save charges by putting God off with the refuse do but deceive themselves, for <hi type="italic">God is not mocked.</hi> 5. All this is given to the priests <hi type="italic">by reason of the anointing,</hi> <reference osisRef="Num.18.8">v. 8</reference>. It was not for the sake of their personal merits above other Israelites that they had these tributes paid to them, be it known unto them; but purely for the sake of the office to which they were anointed. Thus all the comforts that are given to the Lord's people are given them by reason of the anointing which they have received. It is said to be given them <hi type="italic">by an ordinance for ever</hi> (<reference osisRef="Num.18.8">v. 8</reference>), and it is a <hi type="italic">covenant of salt for ever,</hi> <reference osisRef="Num.18.19">v. 19</reference>. As long as the priesthood should continue this should continue to be the maintenance of it, that this lamp might not go out for want of oil to keep it burning. Thus provision is made that a gospel ministry should continue till Christ comes, by an ordinance for ever. <hi type="italic">Lo, I am with you</hi> (that is their maintenance and support) <hi type="italic">always, even to the end of the world.</hi> Thanks be to the Redeemer, it is the word which he has <hi type="italic">commanded to a thousand generations.</hi>
entries.aa96b995a4efeeb4c543ab4fa7551c83e0413d1a: <div eID="gen3050" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Priests and Levites Provided For. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1490.)</title> <div sID="gen3051" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">20</hi> And the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> spake unto Aaron, Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any part among them: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel. <hi type="super">21</hi> And, behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. <hi type="super">22</hi> Neither must the children of Israel henceforth come nigh the tabernacle of the congregation, lest they bear sin, and die. <hi type="super">23</hi> But the Levites shall do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, and they shall bear their iniquity: <hi type="italic">it shall be</hi> a statute for ever throughout your generations, that among the children of Israel they have no inheritance. <hi type="super">24</hi> But the tithes of the children of Israel, which they offer <hi type="italic">as</hi> an heave offering unto the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , I have given to the Levites to inherit: therefore I have said unto them, Among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance. <hi type="super">25</hi> And the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> spake unto Moses, saying, <hi type="super">26</hi> Thus speak unto the Levites, and say unto them, When ye take of the children of Israel the tithes which I have given you from them for your inheritance, then ye shall offer up an heave offering of it for the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , <hi type="italic">even</hi> a tenth <hi type="italic">part</hi> of the tithe. <hi type="super">27</hi> And <hi type="italic">this</hi> your heave offering shall be reckoned unto you, as though <hi type="italic">it were</hi> the corn of the threshingfloor, and as the fulness of the winepress. <hi type="super">28</hi> Thus ye also shall offer an heave offering unto the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> of all your tithes, which ye receive of the children of Israel; and ye shall give thereof the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> 's heave offering to Aaron the priest. <hi type="super">29</hi> Out of all your gifts ye shall offer every heave offering of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , of all the best thereof, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the hallowed part thereof out of it. <hi type="super">30</hi> Therefore thou shalt say unto them, When ye have heaved the best thereof from it, then it shall be counted unto the Levites as the increase of the threshingfloor, and as the increase of the winepress. <hi type="super">31</hi> And ye shall eat it in every place, ye and your households: for it <hi type="italic">is</hi> your reward for your service in the tabernacle of the congregation. <hi type="super">32</hi> And ye shall bear no sin by reason of it, when ye have heaved from it the best of it: neither shall ye pollute the holy things of the children of Israel, lest ye die. <div eID="gen3051" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3052" type="x-p"/> Here is a further account of the provision that was made both for the Levites and for the priests, out of the country. <div eID="gen3052" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3053" type="x-p"/> I. They must have <hi type="italic">no inheritance in the land;</hi> only cities to dwell in were afterwards allowed them, but no ground to occupy: <hi type="italic">Thou shalt not have any part among them,</hi> <reference osisRef="Num.18.20">v. 20</reference>. It is repeated again <reference osisRef="Num.18.23">v. 23</reference>, and again <reference osisRef="Num.18.24">v. 24</reference>, <hi type="italic">Among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance,</hi> either by purchase or descent. God would have them comfortably provided for, but would not have their families over-rich, lest they should think themselves above that work which their wages supposed and obliged them constantly to attend upon. As Israel was a peculiar people, and not to be numbered among the nations, so Levi was a peculiar tribe, and not to be settled as the rest of the tribes, but in all respects distinguished from them. A good reason is given why they must have <hi type="italic">no inheritance in the land,</hi> for, says God, <hi type="italic">I am thy part, and thy inheritance.</hi> Note, Those that have God for their inheritance and their portion for ever ought to look with a holy contempt and indifference upon the inheritances of this world, and not covet their portion in it. "<hi type="italic">The Lord is my portion, therefore will I hope in him,</hi> and not depend upon any thing I have on this earth," <reference osisRef="Lam.3.24">Lam. iii. 24</reference>. The Levites shall have no inheritance, and yet they shall live very comfortably and plentifully—to teach us that Providence has various ways of supporting those that live in a dependence upon it; the fowls reap not, and yet are fed, the lilies spin not, and yet are clothed, the Levites have no inheritance in Israel, and yet live better than any other tribe. The repetition of that caution, that <hi type="italic">no Israelite should approach the tabernacle,</hi> comes in suitable, though somewhat abruptly, <reference osisRef="Num.18.22">v. 22</reference>. It seems set in opposition to that order concerning the priests and Levites that they should have <hi type="italic">no inheritance in Israel,</hi> to show how God dispenses his favours variously. The Levites have the honour of attending the tabernacle, which is denied the Israelites; but then the Israelites have the honour of inheritances in Canaan, which is denied the Levites; thus each is kept from either envying or despising the other, and both have reason to rejoice in their lot. The Israelites must not <hi type="italic">come nigh the tabernacle,</hi> but then the Levites must have <hi type="italic">no inheritance in the land;</hi> if ministers expect that people should keep in their sphere, and not intermeddle with sacred offices, let them keep in theirs, and not entangle themselves in secular affairs. <div eID="gen3053" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3054" type="x-p"/> II. But they must both have tithes of the land. Besides the first-fruits which were appropriated to the priests, which, the Jews say, were to be a fiftieth part, or at least a sixtieth, the tithe also was appropriated. 1. The Levites had the tithes of the people's increase (<reference osisRef="Num.18.21">v. 21</reference>): <hi type="italic">I have given</hi> (whose the whole is) <hi type="italic">all the tenths in Israel,</hi> of all the productions of the land, to <hi type="italic">the children of Levi,</hi> to be divided among them in just proportions, <hi type="italic">for their service which they serve.</hi> The Levites were the smallest tribe of the twelve, and yet, besides all other advantages, they had a tenth part of the yearly profits, without the trouble and expense of ploughing and sowing; such care did God take of those that were devoted to his service; not only that they might be well maintained, but that they might be honoured with a national acknowledgment of the good services they did to the public, and owned as God's agents and receivers; for that which was a heave-offering, or an offering lifted heavenward unto the Lord, was by him consigned to the Levites. 2. The priests had the tenths of the Levites' tithes settled upon them. The order for this Moses is directed to give to the Levites, whom God would have to pay it with cheerfulness, rather than the priests to demand it with authority: <hi type="italic">Speak to the Levites</hi> that it be <hi type="italic">offered by them,</hi> rather than levied upon them. Now observe, (1.) The Levites were to give God his dues out of their tithes, as well as the Israelites out of their increase. They were God's tenants, and rent was expected from them, nor were they exempted by their office. Thus now, ministers must be charitable out of what they receive; and the more freely they have received the more freely they must give, and be examples of liberality. <hi type="italic">You shall offer a heave-offering to the Lord,</hi> <reference osisRef="Num.18.26">v. 26</reference>. Those that are employed to assist the devotions of others must be sure to pay their own, as a heave-offering to the Lord. Prayers and praises lifted up to God, or rather the heart lifted up in them, are now our heave-offerings. This (says God) shall be <hi type="italic">reckoned to you as though it were the corn of the threshing-floor;</hi> that is, though it was not the fruit of their ground, nor of their own labour, as the tithes of other Israelites were, yet being of such as they had it should be accepted, to the sanctifying of all the rest. (2.) This was to be given <hi type="italic">to Aaron the priest</hi> (<reference osisRef="Num.18.28">v. 28</reference>), and to his successors the high priests, to be divided and disposed of in such proportions as they should think fit among the inferior priests. Most of the profits of the priests' office, which were appointed in the former part of the chapter, arising from the sacrifices, those priests had the benefit of who constantly attended at the altar; but, forasmuch as there were many priests employed in the country to teach and rule, those tithes taken by the Levites, it is probable, were directed by the high priest for their maintenance. It is the probable conjecture of the learned bishop Patrick that the tenth of this last tenth was reserved for the high priest himself, to support his state and dignity; for otherwise we read not of any peculiar provision made for him. (3.) When the Levites had thus paid the tenth of their income, as a heave-offering to the Lord, they had themselves the comfortable enjoyment of the other nine parts (<reference osisRef="Num.18.30">v. 30</reference>): "When you have thus <hi type="italic">heaved the best from it</hi> (for still God's part must be the best) then you shall <hi type="italic">eat the rest,</hi> not as a holy thing, but with the same freedom that the other Israelites eat their part with, <hi type="italic">in every place, you and your households,</hi>" <reference osisRef="Num.18.31">v. 31</reference>. See here what is the way to have the comfort of all our worldly possessions so as to bear no sin by reason of them, as it follows, <reference osisRef="Num.18.32">v. 32</reference>. [1.] We must be sure that what we have be got honestly and in the service of God. It is <hi type="italic">your reward for your service;</hi> that meat is the best eating that is first earned; but, if any <hi type="italic">will not work, neither shall he eat,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Thess.3.10">2 Thess. iii. 10</reference>. And that seems to be spoken of as having a particular comfort and satisfaction in it which is the reward of faithful service done in the tabernacle of the congregation. [2.] We must be sure that God has his dues out of it. Then we have the comfort of our substance when we have honoured the Lord with it. The <hi type="italic">you shall bear no sin by reason of it,</hi> when <hi type="italic">you have heaved the best from it.</hi> This intimates that we must never feed ourselves without fear, lest our table become a snare, and we bear sin by reason of it; and that therefore we are concerned to <hi type="italic">give alms of such things as we have,</hi> that all may be clean and comfortable to us.  <chapter eID="Num.18"/> <div eID="gen3054" type="x-p"/>

entries.621e18a975955d41c31715321b8c3fc672205627: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1432"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 18</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Num.18.1-Num.18.7">Nu 18:1-7</reference>. The Charge of the Priests and Levites.</title> <div sID="gen1929" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1432"/><hi type="bold">1. the Lord said unto Aaron, Thou and thy sons and thy father's house with thee shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary--</hi>Security is here given to the people from the fears expressed (<reference osisRef="Num.17.12">Nu 17:12</reference>), by the responsibility of attending to all sacred things being devolved upon the priesthood, together with the penalties incurred through neglect; and thus the solemn responsibilities annexed to their high dignity, of having to answer not only for their own sins, but also for the sins of the people, were calculated in a great measure to remove all feeling of envy at the elevation of Aaron's family, when the honor was weighed in the balance with its burdens and dangers. <div eID="gen1929" type="x-p"/>
entries.6199e3b31b9cdc4694a3c6873a79253c8f6e9ea7: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1433"/><div sID="gen1930" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1433"/><hi type="bold">2-7. thy brethren also of the tribe of Levi--</hi>The departments of the sacred office, to be filled respectively by the priests and Levites, are here assigned to each. To the priests was committed the charge of the sanctuary and the altar, while the Levites were to take care of everything else about the tabernacle. The Levites were to attend the priests as servants--bestowed on them as "gifts" to aid in the service of the tabernacle--while the high and dignified office of the priesthood was a "service of gift." "A stranger," that is, one, neither a priest nor a Levite, who should intrude into any departments of the sacred office, should incur the penalty of death. <div eID="gen1930" type="x-p"/>
entries.e3b14e8f102d71d21446aac2a87c047fc13b671e: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1434"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Num.18.8-Num.18.20">Nu 18:8-20</reference>. The Priests' Portion.</title> <div sID="gen1931" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1434"/><hi type="bold">8-13. the Lord spake unto Aaron, Behold, I also have given thee the charge of my heave offerings--</hi>A recapitulation is made in this passage of certain perquisites specially appropriated to the maintenance of the priests. They were parts of the votive and freewill offerings, including both meat and bread, wine and oil, and the first-fruits, which formed a large and valuable item. <div eID="gen1931" type="x-p"/>
entries.ac1950705cd0bad7ce5c2d545491dbe3118605f6: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1435"/><div sID="gen1932" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1435"/><hi type="bold">14. Every thing devoted in Israel shall be thine--</hi>provided it was adapted for food or consumable by use; for the gold and silver vessels that were dedicated as the spoils of victory were not given to the priests, but for the use and adornment of the sacred edifice. <div eID="gen1932" type="x-p"/>
entries.34faf1bd7eb0879550d08ab7f6c467a0dd9d65bb: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1436"/><div sID="gen1933" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1436"/><hi type="bold">19. it is a covenant of salt--</hi>that is, a perpetual ordinance. This figurative form of expression was evidently founded on the conservative property of salt, which keeps meat from corruption; and hence it became an emblem of inviolability and permanence. It is a common phrase among Oriental people, who consider the eating of salt a pledge of fidelity, binding them in a covenant of friendship. Hence the partaking of the altar meats, which were appropriated to the priests on condition of their services and of which salt formed a necessary accompaniment, was naturally called "a covenant of salt" (<reference osisRef="Lev.2.13">Le 2:13</reference>). <div eID="gen1933" type="x-p"/>
entries.298f4ba3e78bd24bde6464ba6229001b8b1df27c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1437"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Num.18.21-Num.18.32">Nu 18:21-32</reference>. The Levites' Portion.</title> <div sID="gen1934" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1437"/><hi type="bold">21-22. I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for their service which they serve--</hi>Neither the priests nor the Levites were to possess any allotments of land but to depend entirely upon Him who liberally provided for them out of His own portion; and this law was subservient to many important purposes--such as that, being exempted from the cares and labors of worldly business, they might be exclusively devoted to His service; that a bond of mutual love and attachment might be formed between the people and the Levites, who, as performing religious services for the people, derived their subsistence from them; and further, that being the more easily dispersed among the different tribes, they might be more useful in instructing and directing the people. <div eID="gen1934" type="x-p"/>
entries.ab9a7816ecade446082e729f702123a09d6efecb: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1438"/><div sID="gen1935" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1438"/><hi type="bold">23. But the Levites shall do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation: they shall bear their iniquity--</hi>They were to be responsible for the right discharge of those duties that were assigned to them, and consequently to bear the penalty that was due to negligence or carelessness in the guardianship of the holy things. <div eID="gen1935" type="x-p"/>
entries.71a0cd89f3e3d2be8fab02bf099c2177c2ce0d99: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1439"/><div sID="gen1936" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1439"/><hi type="bold">26. the Levites ... offer ... a tenth of the tithe--</hi>Out of their own they were to pay tithes to the priests equally as the people gave to them. The best of their tithes was to be assigned to the priests, and afterwards they enjoyed the same liberty to make use of the remainder that other Israelites had of the produce of their threshing-floors and wine-presses. <div eID="gen1936" type="x-p"/>
entries.77ba093cc37226d85e13c525d7692e6412a0d882: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1440"/><div sID="gen1937" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1440"/><hi type="bold">32. ye shall bear no sin by reason of it, &c.--</hi>Neglect in having the best entailed sin in the use of such unhallowed food. And the holy things would be polluted by the reservation to themselves of what should be offered to God and the priests. <chapter eID="Num.18"/>

entries.64d6c3efc1f2012b30821b20e8c5e4c8e2b0d1c3: <div eID="gen5672" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen5673" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen5674" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5674" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen5673" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen5675" type="x-p"/> The priests are to bear the iniquity of the sanctuary, <reference osisRef="Num.18.1">Num 18:1</reference>. The Levites to minister to the priests, and have charge of the tabernacle, <reference osisRef="Num.18.2-Num.18.4">Num 18:2-4</reference>. The priests alone to have the charge of the sanctuary, etc., no stranger to come nigh on pain of death, <reference osisRef="Num.18.5-Num.18.7">Num 18:5-7</reference> The portion allowed for their maintenance, <reference osisRef="Num.18.8">Num 18:8</reference>. They shall have every meat-offering; and they shall eat them in the holy place, <reference osisRef="Num.18.9">Num 18:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.18.10">Num 18:10</reference>. The wave-offerings, <reference osisRef="Num.18.11">Num 18:11</reference>. The first-fruits of the oil, wine, and wheat, and whatever is first ripe, and every devoted thing, <reference osisRef="Num.18.12-Num.18.14">Num 18:12-14</reference>; also, all the first-born of men and beasts, <reference osisRef="Num.18.15-Num.18.18">Num 18:15-18</reference>; and heave-offerings, <reference osisRef="Num.18.19">Num 18:19</reference>. The priests shall have no inheritance, <reference osisRef="Num.18.20">Num 18:20</reference>. The Levites shall have no inheritance, but shall have the tenth of the produce in Israel, <reference osisRef="Num.18.21-Num.18.24">Num 18:21-24</reference>, of which they are to give a tenth to the priests, taken from the best parts, <reference osisRef="Num.18.25-Num.18.30">Num 18:25-30</reference>. <div eID="gen5675" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5676" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen5676" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5677" type="x-p"/> Thou and thy sons - shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary, etc. - That is, They must be answerable for its legal pollutions, and must make the necessary atonements and expiations. By this they must feel that though they had got a high and important office confirmed to them by a miraculous interference, yet it was a place of the highest responsibility; and that they must not be high-minded, but fear.
entries.ccf27f02c4b3361ee11d034e63823d6dd8b49b15: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen5677" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5678" type="x-p"/> Thy brethren also of the tribe of Levi - may be joined unto thee - There is a fine paronomasia, or play upon words, in the original. לוי Levi comes from the root לוה lavah, to join to, couple, associate: hence Moses says, the Levites, ילוו yillavu, shall be joined, or associated with the priests; they shall conjointly perform the whole of the sacred office, but the priests shall be principal, the Levites only their associates or assistants.
entries.1585d59e6346c293499d63e9f3dc319977100887: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen5678" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5679" type="x-p"/> The first-born of man - and the firstling of unclean beasts - Thus vain man is ranked with the beasts that perish; and with the worst kinds of them too, those deemed unclean.
entries.ecc3e4f19e506101e3dfcb50b8b78c6a0564440b: <hi type="bold">Verse 16</hi> <div eID="gen5679" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5680" type="x-p"/> Shalt thou redeem - for the money of five shekels - Redemption of the first-born is one of the rites which is still practiced among the Jews. According to Leo of Modena, it is performed in the following manner: - <div eID="gen5680" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5681" type="x-p"/> When the child is thirty days old, the father sends for one of the descendants of Aaron: several persons being assembled on the occasion, the father brings a cup containing several pieces of gold and silver coin. The priest then takes the child into his arms, and addressing himself to the mother, says: Is this thy son? <div eID="gen5681" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5682" type="x-p"/> Mother. Yes. <div eID="gen5682" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5683" type="x-p"/> Priest. Hast thou never had another child, male or female, a miscarriage or untimely birth? <div eID="gen5683" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5684" type="x-p"/> Mother. No. <div eID="gen5684" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5685" type="x-p"/> Priest. This being the case, this child, as first-born, belongs to me. <div eID="gen5685" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5686" type="x-p"/> Then, turning to the father, he says: If it be thy desire to have this child, thou must redeem it. <div eID="gen5686" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5687" type="x-p"/> Father. I present thee with this gold and silver for this purpose. <div eID="gen5687" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5688" type="x-p"/> Priest. Thou dost wish, therefore, to redeem the child? <div eID="gen5688" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5689" type="x-p"/> Father. I do wish so to do. <div eID="gen5689" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5690" type="x-p"/> The priest then, turning himself to the assembly, says: Very well; this child, as first-born, is mine, as it is written in Bemidbar, (<reference osisRef="Num.18.16">Num 18:16</reference>), Thou shalt redeem the first-born of a month old for five shekels, but I shall content myself with this in exchange. He then takes two gold crowns, or thereabouts, and returns the child to his parents.
entries.b0e879477c50d020aa3a8c98cbc7c73b087b6864: <hi type="bold">Verse 19</hi> <div eID="gen5690" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5691" type="x-p"/> It is a covenant of salt - That is, an incorruptible, everlasting covenant. As salt was added to different kinds of viands, not only to give them a relish, but to preserve them from putrefaction and decay, it became the emblem of incorruptibility and permanence. Hence, a covenant of salt signified an everlasting covenant. We have already seen that, among the Asiatics, eating together was deemed a bond of perpetual friendship; and as salt was a common article in all their repasts, it may be in reference to this circumstance that a perpetual covenant is termed a covenant of salt; because the parties ate together of the sacrifice offered on the occasion, and the whole transaction was considered as a league of endless friendship. See the note on <reference osisRef="Lev.2.13">Lev 2:13</reference>.
entries.3635191a3970f331dc636333e988a3215eafc62e: <hi type="bold">Verse 20</hi> <div eID="gen5691" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5692" type="x-p"/> I am thy part and thine inheritance - The principal part of what was offered to God was the portion of the priests, therefore they had no inheritance of land in Israel; independently of that they had a very ample provision for their support. The rabbins say twenty-four gifts were given to the priests, and they are all expressed in the law. Eight of those gifts the priests ate nowhere but in the sanctuary: these eight are the following: - <div eID="gen5692" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5693" type="x-p"/> 1. The flesh of the Sin-Offering, whether of beasts or fowls, <reference osisRef="Lev.6.25">Lev 6:25</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.6.26">Lev 6:26</reference>. <div eID="gen5693" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5694" type="x-p"/> 2. The flesh of the Trespass-Offering, <reference osisRef="Lev.7.1">Lev 7:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.7.6">Lev 7:6</reference>. <div eID="gen5694" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5695" type="x-p"/> 3. The Peace-Offerings of the congregation, <reference osisRef="Lev.23.19">Lev 23:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.23.20">Lev 23:20</reference>. <div eID="gen5695" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5696" type="x-p"/> 4. The remainder of the Omer or Sheaf, <reference osisRef="Lev.23.10">Lev 23:10</reference>, etc. <div eID="gen5696" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5697" type="x-p"/> 5. The remnants of the Meat-Offerings of the Israelites, <reference osisRef="Lev.6.16">Lev 6:16</reference>. <div eID="gen5697" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5698" type="x-p"/> 6. The two Loaves, <reference osisRef="Lev.23.17">Lev 23:17</reference>. <div eID="gen5698" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5699" type="x-p"/> 7. The Shew-Bread, <reference osisRef="Lev.24.9">Lev 24:9</reference>. <div eID="gen5699" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5700" type="x-p"/> 8. The Log of oil offered by the leper, <reference osisRef="Lev.14.10">Lev 14:10</reference>, etc. <div eID="gen5700" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5701" type="x-p"/> Five of those gifts they ate only in Jerusalem: - <div eID="gen5701" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5702" type="x-p"/> 1. The breast and shoulder of the Peace-Offerings, <reference osisRef="Lev.7.31">Lev 7:31</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.7.34">Lev 7:34</reference>. <div eID="gen5702" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5703" type="x-p"/> 2. The Heave-Offering of the sacrifice of confession, <reference osisRef="Lev.7.12-Lev.7.14">Lev 7:12-14</reference>. <div eID="gen5703" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5704" type="x-p"/> 3. The Heave-Offering of the Nazarite's ram, <reference osisRef="Lev.6.17-Lev.6.20">Lev 6:17-20</reference>. <div eID="gen5704" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5705" type="x-p"/> 4. The Firstling of the clean beast, <reference osisRef="Num.18.15">Num 18:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deu.15.19">Deu 15:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deu.15.20">Deu 15:20</reference>. <div eID="gen5705" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5706" type="x-p"/> 5. The First-Fruits, <reference osisRef="Num.18.13">Num 18:13</reference>. <div eID="gen5706" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5707" type="x-p"/> Five gifts were not due unto them by the law, but in the land of Israel only: - <div eID="gen5707" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5708" type="x-p"/> 1. The heave-offering or First-Fruits, <reference osisRef="Num.18.12">Num 18:12</reference>. <div eID="gen5708" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5709" type="x-p"/> 2. The heave-offering of the Tithe, <reference osisRef="Num.18.28">Num 18:28</reference>. <div eID="gen5709" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5710" type="x-p"/> 3. The Cake, <reference osisRef="Num.15.20">Num 15:20</reference>. <div eID="gen5710" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5711" type="x-p"/> These three were holy. <div eID="gen5711" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5712" type="x-p"/> 4. The first-fruits of the Fleece, <reference osisRef="Deu.18.4">Deu 18:4</reference>. <div eID="gen5712" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5713" type="x-p"/> 5. The Field of Possession, Numbers 35. <div eID="gen5713" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5714" type="x-p"/> These two were common. <div eID="gen5714" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5715" type="x-p"/> Five gifts were due unto them both within and without the land: - <div eID="gen5715" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5716" type="x-p"/> 1. The gifts of the Beasts Slain, <reference osisRef="Deu.18.3">Deu 18:3</reference>. <div eID="gen5716" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5717" type="x-p"/> 2. The redemption of the First-Born Son, <reference osisRef="Num.18.15">Num 18:15</reference>. <div eID="gen5717" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5718" type="x-p"/> 3. The Lamb for the firstling of an ass, <reference osisRef="Exo.4.20">Exo 4:20</reference>; Numbers 18. <div eID="gen5718" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5719" type="x-p"/> 4. The restitution of that taken by violence from a stranger, <reference osisRef="Num.5.8">Num 5:8</reference>. <div eID="gen5719" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5720" type="x-p"/> 5. All Devoted things, <reference osisRef="Num.18.14">Num 18:14</reference>. <div eID="gen5720" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5721" type="x-p"/> One gift was due unto them from the sanctuary: - <div eID="gen5721" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5722" type="x-p"/> 1. The skins of the burnt-offering, and all the skins of the other most holy things, <reference osisRef="Lev.7.8">Lev 7:8</reference>. <div eID="gen5722" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5723" type="x-p"/> In all 24. See Ainsworth. <div eID="gen5723" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5724" type="x-p"/> The gifts which the females of the priests' families had a part in were these: - <div eID="gen5724" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5725" type="x-p"/> 1. The heave-offering, or first-fruits. <div eID="gen5725" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5726" type="x-p"/> 2. The heave-offering of the tithe. <div eID="gen5726" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5727" type="x-p"/> 3. The cake. <div eID="gen5727" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5728" type="x-p"/> 4. The gifts of the beast, <reference osisRef="Deu.18.3">Deu 18:3</reference>. <div eID="gen5728" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5729" type="x-p"/> 5. The first of the fleece. - See Mishna, Tract. Biccurim, and Ainsworth on the Pentateuch. <div eID="gen5729" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5730" type="x-p"/> Besides all this the priests had the tribute money mentioned <reference osisRef="Num.31.28">Num 31:28</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.31.29">Num 31:29</reference>.
entries.0ee1c7d8ed460db4272b0fe2d7e996d681d6a878: <hi type="bold">Verse 21</hi> <div eID="gen5730" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5731" type="x-p"/> Behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth - <div eID="gen5731" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5732" type="x-p"/> 1. The Levites had the tenth of all the productions of the land. <div eID="gen5732" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5733" type="x-p"/> 2. They had forty-eight cities, each forming a square of 4,000 cubits. <div eID="gen5733" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5734" type="x-p"/> 3. They had 2,000 cubits of ground round each city. Total of the land they possessed, 53,000 acres. <div eID="gen5734" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5735" type="x-p"/> 4. They had the first-fruits and certain parts of all the animals killed in the land. <div eID="gen5735" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5736" type="x-p"/> Canaan contained about 11,264,000 acres; therefore the portion possessed by the Levites was rather less than as one to two hundred and twelve; for 11,264,000 divided by 53,000, quotes only 212 28/53 - See Lowman, Dodd, etc. But though this was a very small proportion for a whole tribe that had consented to annihilate its political existence, that it might wait upon the service of God, and labor for the people's souls; yet let it be considered that what they possessed was the best of the land: and while it was a slender remuneration for their services, yet their portion was such as rendered them independent, and kept them comfortable; so that they could wait on the Lord's work without distraction. This is a proper pattern for the maintenance of the ministers of God: let them have a sufficiency for themselves and families, that there may be no distracting cares; and let them not be encumbered with riches or worldly possessions, that they may not be prevented from taking care of souls.
entries.af52c18e3b9af7af11126ab74b706dff04a01e00: <hi type="bold">Verse 28</hi> <div eID="gen5736" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5737" type="x-p"/> Thus ye also shall offer a heave-offering - As the Levites had the tithe of the whole land, they themselves were obliged to give the tithe of this tithe to the priests, so that this considerably lessened their revenue. And this tithe or tenth they were obliged to select from the best part of the substance they had received, <reference osisRef="Num.18.29">Num 18:29</reference>, etc. A portion of all must be given to God, as an evidence of his goodness, and their dependence on him. See the end at <reference osisRef="Num.20.28">Num 20:28</reference>.  <chapter eID="Num.18"/> <div eID="gen5737" type="x-p"/>

entries.bfbaae01cfca92498a7250d3f22b2710bde53e4a: Service and Revenues of the Priests and Levites - Numbers 18 <div eID="gen1825" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1826" type="x-p"/> The practical confirmation of the priesthood of Aaron and his family, on the part of God, is very appropriately followed by the legal regulations concerning the official duties of the priest and Levites (Num 18:1-7), and the revenues to be assigned them for their services (vv. 8-32), as the laws hitherto given upon this subject, although they contain many isolated stipulations, have not laid down any complete and comprehensive arrangement. The instructions relating to this subject were addressed by Jehovah directly to Aaron (see Num 18:1 and Num 18:8), up to the law, that out of the tenths which the Levites were to collect from the people, they were to pay a tenth again to the priests; and this was addressed to Moses (Num 18:25), as the head of all Israel. <div eID="gen1826" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1827" type="x-p"/> The Official Duties and Rights of the Priests and Levites. - Num 18:1. To impress upon the minds of the priests and Levites the holiness and responsibility of their office, the service of Aaron, of his sons, and of his father’s house, i.e., of the family of the Kohathites, is described as “bearing the iniquity of the sanctuary,” and the service which was peculiar to the Aaronides, as “bearing the iniquity of their priesthood.” “<hi type="italic">To bear the iniquity of the sanctuary</hi>” signifies not only “to have to make expiation for all that offended against the laws of the priests and the holy things, i.e., the desecration of these” (<hi type="italic">Knobel</hi>), but “iniquity or transgression at the sanctuary,” i.e., the defilement of it by the sin of those who drew near to the sanctuary; not only of the priests and Levites, but of the whole people who defiled the sanctuary in the midst of them with its holy vessels, not only by their sins (<reference osisRef="Lev.16.6">Lev 16:6</reference>), but even by their holy gifts (<reference osisRef="Exod.28.38">Exo 28:38</reference>), and thus brought guilt upon the whole congregation, which the priests were to bear, i.e., to take upon themselves and expunge, by virtue of the holiness and sanctifying power communicated to their office (see at <reference osisRef="Exod.28.38">Exo 28:38</reference>). The “iniquity of the priesthood,” however, not only embraced every offence against the priesthood, every neglect of the most scrupulous and conscientious fulfilment of duty in connection with their office, but extended to all the sin which attached to the official acts of the priests, on account of the sinfulness of their nature. It was to wipe out these sins and defilements, that the annual expiation of the holy things on the day of atonement had been appointed (Lev 16:16.). The father’s house of Aaron, i.e., the Levitical family of Kohath, was also to join in bearing the iniquity of the sanctuary, because the oversight of the holy vessels of the sanctuary devolved upon it (Num 4:4).
entries.6c7dd92375a27539e2d5f297805e065402ebbedb: Num 18:2-4 <div eID="gen1827" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1828" type="x-p"/> Aaron was also to bring his (other) brethren (sc., to the sanctuary), viz., the tribe of Levi, that is to say, the Gershonites and Merarites, that they might attach themselves to him and serve him, both him (ואתּה) and his sons, before the tent of testimony, and discharge the duties that were binding upon them, according to Num 4:24., Num 4:31. (cf. Num 3:6-7; Num 8:26). Only they were not to come near to the holy vessels and the altar, for that would bring death both upon them and the priests (see at Num 4:15). On Num 18:4, cf. Num 1:53 and Num 3:7.
entries.052935ca4a53d8e8dc7ee46e9a3560cf8042ecf1: Num 18:5-7 <div eID="gen1828" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1829" type="x-p"/> The charge of the sanctuary (i.e., the dwelling) and the altar (of burnt-offering) devolved upon Aaron and his sons, that the wrath of God might not come again upon the children of Israel (see Num 8:19), - namely, through such illegal acts as Nadab and Abihu (<reference osisRef="Lev.10.2">Lev 10:2</reference>), and the company of Korah (Num 16:35), had committed. To this end God had handed over the Levites to them as a gift, to be their assistants (see at Num 3:9 and Num 8:16, Num 8:19). But Aaron and his sons were to attend to the priesthood “<hi type="italic">with regard to everything of the altar and within the vail</hi>” (i.e., of the most holy place, see <reference osisRef="Lev.16.12">Lev 16:12</reference>). The allusion is to all the priestly duties from the altar of burnt-offering to the most holy place, including the holy place which lay between. This office, which brought them into the closest fellowship with the Lord, was a favour accorded to them by the grace of God. This is expressed in the words, “<hi type="italic">as a service of gift</hi> (a service with which I present you) <hi type="italic">I give you the priesthood</hi>.” The last words in Num 18:7 are the same as in Num 1:51; and “<hi type="italic">stranger</hi>” (<hi type="italic">zar</hi>), as in Lev 22:10.
entries.ca254f0ae2f9a70ef4a18cb315b9d22550831702: Num 18:8-18 <div eID="gen1829" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1830" type="x-p"/> The Revenues of the Priests. - These are summed up in Num 18:8 in these words, “<hi type="italic">I give thee the keeping of My heave-offerings in all holy gifts for a portion, as an eternal statute</hi>.” The notion of משׁמרת, keeping, as in <reference osisRef="Exod.12.6">Exo 12:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.16.23">Exo 16:23</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.16.32">Exo 16:32</reference>, is defined in the second parallel clause as משׁחה, a portion (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.7.35">Lev 7:35</reference>). The priests were to keep all the heave-offerings, as the portion which belonged to them, out of the sacrificial gifts that the children of Israel offered to the Lord. תּרוּמת, heave-offerings (see at <reference osisRef="Exod.25.2">Exo 25:2</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Lev.2.9">Lev 2:9</reference>), is used here in the broadest sense, as including all the holy gifts (<hi type="italic">kodashim</hi>, see <reference osisRef="Lev.21.22">Lev 21:22</reference>) which the Israelites lifted off from their possessions and presented to the Lord (as in Num 5:9). Among these, for example, were, <hi type="italic">first</hi> of all, the most holy gifts in the meat-offerings, sin-offerings, and trespass-offerings (Num 18:9, Num 18:10; see at <reference osisRef="Lev.2.3">Lev 2:3</reference>). The burnt-offerings are not mentioned, because the whole of the flesh of these was burned upon the altar, and the skin alone fell to the portion of the priest (<reference osisRef="Lev.7.8">Lev 7:8</reference>). “<hi type="italic">From the fire,</hi>” sc., of the altar. אשׁ, fire, is equivalent to אשּׁה ot , firing (see <reference osisRef="Lev.1.9">Lev 1:9</reference>). These gifts they were to eat, as most holy, in a most holy place, i.e., in the court of the tabernacle (see <reference osisRef="Lev.6.9">Lev 6:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.6.19">Lev 6:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.7.6">Lev 7:6</reference>), which is called “<hi type="italic">most holy</hi>” here, to lay a stronger emphasis upon the precept. In the second place, these gifts included also “<hi type="italic">the holy gifts;</hi>” viz., (<hi type="italic">a</hi>) (Num 18:11) the heave-offering of their gifts in all wave-offerings (<hi type="italic">tenuphoth</hi>), i.e., the wave-breast and heave-leg of the peace-offerings, and whatever else was waved in connection with the sacrifices (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.7.33">Lev 7:33</reference>): these might be eaten by both the male and female members of the priestly families, provided they were legally clean (Lev 22:3.); (<hi type="italic">b</hi>) (Num 18:12) the gifts of first-fruits: “<hi type="italic">all the fat</hi> (i.e., the best, as in <reference osisRef="Gen.45.18">Gen 45:18</reference>) <hi type="italic">of oil, new wine, and corn,</hi>” viz., ראשׁיתם, “<hi type="italic">the first of them</hi>,” the בּכּוּרים, “<hi type="italic">the first-grown fruits</hi>” of the land, and that of all the fruit of the ground (<reference osisRef="Deut.26.2">Deu 26:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.26.10">Deu 26:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.3.9">Pro 3:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.44.30">Eze 44:30</reference>), corn, wine, oil, honey, and tree-fruit (<reference osisRef="Deut.8.8">Deu 8:8</reference>, compared with <reference osisRef="Lev.19.23-Lev.19.24">Lev 19:23-24</reference>), which were offered, according to <reference osisRef="2Chr.31.5">2Ch 31:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Neh.10.36">Neh 10:36</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.10.38">Neh 10:38</reference>, Tob. 1:6, as first-fruits every year (see <hi type="italic">Mishnah, Bikkur,</hi> i. 3, 10, where the first-fruits are specified according to the productions mentioned in <reference osisRef="Deut.8.8">Deu 8:8</reference>; the law prescribed nothing in relation to the quantity of the different first-fruits, but left this entirely to the offerer himself); (<hi type="italic">c</hi>) (Num 18:14) everything placed under a ban (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.27.28">Lev 27:28</reference>); and (<hi type="italic">d</hi>) (Num 18:15-18) the first-born of man and beast. The first-born of men and of unclean beasts were redeemed according to Num 3:47; <reference osisRef="Exod.13.12-Exod.13.13">Exo 13:12-13</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Lev.27.6">Lev 27:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.27.27">Lev 27:27</reference>; but such as were fit for sacrifice were actually offered, the blood being swung against the altar, and the fat portions burned upon it, whilst the whole of the flesh fell to the portion of the priests. So far as the redemption of human beings was concerned (Num 18:16), they were “<hi type="italic">to redeem from the monthly child,</hi>” i.e., the first-born child as soon as it was a month old.
entries.665a968f28dfe6d49aad6ea78b38d6c840b480ee: Num 18:19 <div eID="gen1830" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1831" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">All the holy heave-offerings</hi>” are not the thank-offerings (<hi type="italic">Knobel</hi>), but, as in Num 18:8, all the holy gifts enumerated in Num 18:9-18. Jehovah gives these to the priests as an eternal claim. “<hi type="italic">An eternal covenant of salt is this before Jehovah,</hi>” for Aaron and his descendants. A “covenant of salt;” equivalent to an indissoluble covenant, or inviolable contract (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.2.13">Lev 2:13</reference>).
entries.24042ffe3099d7b9c1d0ab8cf11950bc226b6094: Num 18:20 <div eID="gen1831" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1832" type="x-p"/> For this reason, Aaron was to received no inheritance in the land among the children of Israel. Aaron, as the head of the priests, represents the whole priesthood; and with regard to the possession, the whole tribe of Levi is placed, in Num 18:23, on an equality with the priests. The Levites were to receive no portion of the land as an inheritance in Canaan (cf. Num 26:62; <reference osisRef="Deut.12.12">Deu 12:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.14.27">Deu 14:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.14.3">Jos 14:3</reference>). Jehovah was the portion and inheritance, not only of Aaron and his sons, but of the whole tribe of Levi (cf. <reference osisRef="Deut.10.9">Deu 10:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.18.2">Deu 18:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.13.33">Jos 13:33</reference>); or, as it is expressed in <reference osisRef="Josh.18.7">Jos 18:7</reference>, “the priesthood of Jehovah was their inheritance,” though not in the sense that <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> supposes viz., “the priesthood with its revenues,” which would make the expression “Jehovah, the God of Israel” (<reference osisRef="Josh.13.33">Jos 13:33</reference>), to be metonymical for “sacrificial gifts, first-fruits, and tenths.” The possession of the priests and Levites did not consist in the revenues assigned to them by God, but in the possession of Jehovah, the God of Israel. In the same sense in which the tribe of Levi was the peculiar possession of Jehovah out of the whole of the people of possession, was Jehovah also the peculiar possession of Levi; and just as the other tribes were to live upon what was afforded by the land assigned them as a possession, Levi was to live upon what Jehovah bestowed upon it. And inasmuch as not only the whole land of the twelve tribes, with which Jehovah had enfeoffed them, but the whole earth, belonged to Jehovah (<reference osisRef="Exod.19.5">Exo 19:5</reference>), He was necessarily to be regarded as the greatest possession of all, beyond which nothing greater is conceivable, and in comparison with which every other possession is to be regarded as nothing. Hence it was evidently the greatest privilege and highest honour to have Him for a portion and possession (Bähr,<hi type="italic">Symbolik,</hi> ii. p. 44). “For truly,” as <hi type="italic">Masius</hi> writes (Com. on Josh.), “he who possesses God possesses all things; and the worship (<hi type="italic">cultus</hi>) of Him is infinitely fuller of delight, and far more productive, than the cultivation (<hi type="italic">cultus</hi>) of any soil.”
entries.e4c7e489d01690864d3f26b4bd2e1e6e444245c3: Num 18:21-24 <div eID="gen1832" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1833" type="x-p"/> Revenues of the Levites. - For (חלף, instead of, for) their service at the tabernacle God assigns them “<hi type="italic">every tenth in Israel as an inheritance</hi>.” On the tenth, see at <reference osisRef="Lev.27.30">Lev 27:30</reference>-33. The institution and description of their service in Num 18:22 and Num 18:23 is the same as that in Num 1:53 and Num 8:19. “Lest they bear sin:” see at Lev 19:17.
entries.78cdc08131a6412c32bc5e8011c4e274916bc1bf: Num 18:25-28 <hi type="italic">Appropriation of the Tithe</hi>. - Num 18:26. When the Levites took (received) from the people the tithe assigned them by Jehovah, they were to lift off from it a heave-offering for Jehovah, a tithe of the tithe for Aaron the priest (i.e., for the priesthood; see at Num 18:20). “<hi type="italic">Your heave-offering shall be reckoned to you as the corn of the threshing-floor, and the fulness</hi> (see <reference osisRef="Exod.22.28">Exo 22:28</reference>) <hi type="italic">of the wine-press,</hi>” i.e., according to Num 18:30, as the revenue of the threshing-floor and wine-press; that is to say, as corn and wine which they had reaped themselves.
entries.1d3bb1c6f9af9005a21f51d2ae83d26a2c2b2638: Num 18:29 <div eID="gen1833" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1834" type="x-p"/> The whole of this heave-offering of Jehovah, i.e., the tithe of the tithe, they were to lift off from all their gifts, from all the tithes of the people which they received; “<hi type="italic">of all the fat of it,</hi>” i.e., of all the best of the heave-offering they received, they were to lift off את־מקדּשׁו, “<hi type="italic">its holy,</hi>” i.e., the holy part, which was to be dedicated to Jehovah.
entries.2f25cec923c70d32c48ff0e36c96f1f461070cce: Num 18:30-31 <div eID="gen1834" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1835" type="x-p"/> They might eat it (the tithe they had received, after taking off the priests’ tithe) in any place with their families, as it was the reward for their service at the tabernacle.
entries.a952e9b8dc3b41451354f5659de74c413004388b: Num 18:32 <div eID="gen1835" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1836" type="x-p"/> They would load no sin upon themselves by so doing (see <reference osisRef="Lev.19.17">Lev 19:17</reference>), if they only lifted off the best as tithe (for the priest), and did not desecrate the holy gifts, sc., by eating in all kinds of places, which was not allowed, according to Num 18:10, with regard to the most holy gifts. These regulations concerning the revenues of the priests and Levites were in perfect accordance with the true idea of the Israelitish kingdom of God. Whereas in heathen states, where there was an hereditary priestly caste, that caste was generally a rich one, and held a firm possession in the soil (in Egypt, for example; see at <reference osisRef="Gen.47.22">Gen 47:22</reference>), the Levites received no hereditary landed property in the land of Israel, but only towns to dwell in among the other tribes, with pasturage for their cattle (ch. 35), because Jehovah, the God of Israel, would be their inheritance. In this way their earthly existence as based upon the spiritual ground and soil of faith, in accordance with the calling assigned them to be the guardians and promoters of the commandments, statutes, and rights of Jehovah; and their authority and influence among the people were bound up with their unreserved surrender of themselves to the Lord, and their firm reliance upon the possession of their God. Now, whilst this position was to be a constant incitement to the Levites to surrender themselves entirely to the Lord and His service, it was also to become to the whole nation a constant admonition, inasmuch as it was a prerogative conferred upon them by the Lord, to seek the highest of all good in the possession of the Lord, as its portion and inheritance. - The revenue itself, however, which the Lord assigned to the Levites and priests, as His servants, consisting of the tenths and first-fruits, as well as certain portions of the different sacrificial gifts that were offered to Him, appears to have been a very considerable one, especially if we adopt the computation of J. D. Michaelis (Mos. Recht. i. §52) with reference to the tithes. “A tribe,” he says, “which had only 22,000 males in it (23,000 afterwards), and therefore could hardly have numbered more than 12,000 grown-up men, received the tithes of 600,000 Israelites; consequently one single Levite, without the slightest necessity for sowing, and without any of the expenses of agriculture, reaped or received from the produce of the flocks and herds as much as five of the other Israelites.” But this leaves out of sight the fact that tithes are never paid so exactly as this, and that no doubt there was as little conscientiousness in the matter then as there is at the present day, when those who are entitled to receive a tenth often receive even less than a twentieth. Moreover, the revenue of the tribe, which the Lord had chosen as His own peculiar possession, was not intended to be a miserable and beggarly one; but it was hardly equal, at any time, to the revenues which the priestly castes of other nations derived from their endowments. Again, the Levites had to give up the tenth of all the tithes they received to the priests; and the priests were to offer to Jehovah upon the altar a portion of the first-fruits, heave-offerings, and wave-offerings that were assigned to them. Consequently, as the whole nation was to make a practical acknowledgment, in the presentation of the tithe and first-fruits, that it had received its hereditary property as a fief from the Lord its God, so the Levites, by their payment of the tenth to the priests, and the priests, by presenting a portion of their revenues upon the altar, were to make a practical confession that they had received all their revenues from the Lord their God, and owed Him praise and adoration in return (see Bähr, <hi type="italic">Symbolik</hi>, ii. pp. 43ff.).  <chapter eID="Num.18"/> <div eID="gen1836" type="x-p"/>

entries.8c11c6bb256d856d3d897f37f07a495a61c83ce3: <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.18.1" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Num.18.1" sID="gen12111" type="section"/> <div sID="gen12112" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1</hi> <hi type="italic"> And the Lord said unto Aaron, Thou and thy sons.</hi> By this solemn appeal God stirs up the priests to devote themselves to their duty with the greatest fidelity and zeal, for He declares that if anything should be done contrary to the requirements of religion, they should be accounted guilty of it, since those are said to “bear the iniquity of the sanctuary” who sustain the crime and the punishment of all its pollutions. God would have the sanctuary kept clear from every stain and defect; and also the dignity of the priesthood was to be maintained in chastity and pureness; a heavy burden, therefore, was imposed upon the priests when they were set over the holy things as their guardians, on this condition that if anything were done amiss they were to be exposed to punishment, because the blame rested on them; just as if God had said that negligence alone was tantamount to sacrilege. Thus their honor, conjoined as it was with so much difficulty and danger, was by no means to be envied.<div eID="gen12112" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12113" type="x-p"/>In this way did God admonish them that the legal rites were of no trifling importance, since he so severely avenged all profanations of them; for thus it was easily to be gathered that something far more excellent and altogether divine was to be sought for in these earthly elements. This may also be very properly applied spiritually to all pastors, to whom blame is justly imputed, if religion and the holiness of God’s worship be corrupted, if purity of doctrine impaired, if the welfare of the people endangered, since the care of all these things is entrusted to them.<div eID="gen12113" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.18.1" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen12111" osisID="Num.18.1" type="section"/>
entries.292262ff16456dcb7b221d2b974c0eb81f78704d: <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.18.2" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Num.18.2" sID="gen12114" type="section"/> <div sID="gen12115" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2.</hi> <hi type="italic">And thy brethren also.</hi> He here assigns their duties to the Levites, that they also may minister, but, as it were, under the hand of the priests, viz., that they may be ruled by their commands. Thus the authority was in the hands of the priests, but the Levites afforded them their assistance. On this ground they are prohibited from approaching the altar, or entering the greater sanctuary; in fact, a lower degree is assigned to them, half-way between the priests and the people. Hence did all learn how reverently God’s majesty must be served; for although He had adopted the whole people, yet so far was it from being lawful that any of the multitude should penetrate to the altar, that the Law even kept back the Levites from thence, although they were God’s peculiar ministers. Moreover, in this figure, we perceive how necessary is a Mediator for us to conciliate God’s favor towards us; for, if it was not allowable for the holy and chosen seed of Abraham to approach the typical sanctuary, how should we, who were aliens, <note n="200"> <div sID="gen12116" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="fr">Qui estions estrangers, et rejettez au pris d’eux</foreign>.” —<hi type="italic"> Fr.</hi><div eID="gen12116" type="x-p"/> </note> now penetrate to heaven, unless a way of access were opened to us through Christ? Finally, when He forbids strangers from meddling with holy things, He does not mean only foreigners, but all the people, except the tribe of Levi; for here a distinction is drawn, not between the Church and heathen nations, but between the ministers of the sanctuary and the rest of the people.<div eID="gen12115" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.18.2" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen12114" osisID="Num.18.2" type="section"/>
entries.3bf4b4f6d89c016a525bd5f645a5cc59b1d27c6e: <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.18.5" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Num.18.5" sID="gen12117" type="section"/> <div sID="gen12118" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5.</hi> <hi type="italic">And ye shall keep the charge.</hi> He again exhorts the priests to be diligent in the performance of their office, with the addition of a denunciation of punishment if they failed in zeal and earnestness. Nor does He now threaten them alone, but the whole people; neither does this contradict the foregoing declaration, inasmuch as the common fault of all by no means lightened theirs. Nay, if God punished the innocent people on account of the pollution of the sanctuary, how much heavier a punishment awaited the priests, (<hi type="italic">antistites,</hi>) by whose fault the sin was committed, so that they might be justly accounted its authors. Meanwhile let us learn from this passage how sincerely we ought to demean ourselves in the service of God, the profanation of which is intolerable to Him. Moreover, in order that the priests might engage themselves in their duties more actively, and with greater sedulity, He shews that they cannot give way to idleness without base ingratitude, since they reign in a manner over the whole tribe of Levi, or at any rate they hold the supremacy among their brethren. An indirect reproof of their negligence, if they do not faithfully fulfill their duties, is implied, when God reminds them that He has of His liberality honored them with the priesthood. “I have appointed your office, as a gift,” <note n="201"> <div sID="gen12119" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="la">Donum posui munus vestrum</foreign>.” — <hi type="italic">Lat.</hi> “I have given your office <hi type="italic">unto you as </hi>a service of gift.” — <hi type="italic">A. V.</hi> The latter part of the sentence is omitted in <hi type="italic">Fr.</hi><div eID="gen12119" type="x-p"/> </note> <hi type="italic">i.e., </hi>I have gratuitously conferred on you what was otherwise yours by no right. Others read it differently, viz., “I have appointed your priesthood as a ministration of gift:” but since the meaning amounts to the same thing, nor does it make any difference in the main, we may freely take our choice.<div eID="gen12118" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.18.5" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen12117" osisID="Num.18.5" type="section"/>
entries.89fbac8ffc0b0b55ff5397c29f23127825e903a9: <div annotateRef="Bible:Num.18.8" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Num.18.8" sID="gen12267" type="section"/> <div sID="gen12268" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8.</hi> <hi type="italic">And the Lord spake unto Aaron.</hi> He now proceeds to state more fully what he had been lately adverting to, as to the rights of the priests with respect to the sacred oblations. We must, however, remember the contrast, which I spoke of, between the priests of the higher order and the Levites; for, whilst the family of Aaron is invested with peculiar honors, the other families of the tribe of Levi are abased. God, then, assigns to the priests alone all the offerings, in which was the greater consecration, called “the holy of holinesses.” <note n="208"> <div sID="gen12269" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">A.
